claims.statement: `.agents/skills/` is the canonical project skill tree: each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with Agent Skills YAML frontmatter and Markdown instructions, and the tree is directly read by Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Deep Agents, and other supported agents.

Claude Code consumes `.claude/skills/` rather than the canonical tree; `make skills` creates that directory, symlinks canonical skills without replacing non-symlink personal entries, and removes stale symlinks, whereas local-source installation through the `skills` CLI copies files that must be refreshed after source changes.

The root guide defines derived instruction surfaces: the style guide is mirrored into path-scoped Cursor and GitHub instruction files, while critical rules, repository structure, quick reference, frontmatter, and syntax are summarized in `.cursorrules` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`; changes to covered sections require updates to their copies in the same PR.

A new skill must use a kebab-case directory and matching `name`, a request-oriented description, and one focused workflow; validate the canonical path with `claude plugin validate .agents/skills --strict` because the validator does not follow the Claude symlinks, then keep the README and root Skills catalogues current.

`tests/unit_tests/test_skills.py` structurally validates every canonical skill's frontmatter, supported keys, description length, referenced repository paths, referenced Make targets, and equality between the skill tree and both README and `AGENTS.md` inventories.
The focused skill-contract test runs through the repository test target as `make test TEST_FILE=tests/unit_tests/test_skills.py`.

The `docs-edit` skill protects pull-request ownership by requiring edits for a named PR to land on its head branch, using `gh pr checkout` for a cross-repository PR; it directs authors to inspect the live PR diff and lint changed prose before handoff.

`docs-team-voice` supplements Vale and the root style guide with editorial guidance: it sets sentence-length thresholds, directs authors to link first mentions and state conditions before behavior, requires exact identifiers and verified examples, and finishes with a targeted revision pass and `make lint_prose`.

`docs-tooling-notion` routes tracked tooling changes to exactly one of five Docs Team Notion pages, keeps repository-owned material and complete skill procedures out of Notion, and requires the Notion MCP fetch and update tools.

For Notion updates, `docs-tooling-notion` requires fetching before each edit and narrow `update_content` replacements; it warns against rewriting pages with uploaded images and requires verification before retrying asynchronous or timed-out updates.

The current catalog distinguishes page lifecycle, in-place editing, page-family restructuring, writing and reviewing prose, code samples, source verification, Notion tooling records, and new versus existing integration listing workflows.

`docs-restructure` requires authors to build and report a page-family duplication map before editing, assign one owner per topic, delete duplicate content in favor of a pointer, resolve conflicting facts against source, and hand lifecycle mechanics to `add-docs-page`.

`docs-review` resolves a PR, branch, or current working-tree target before inspection, limits review to changed source Markdown or MDX rather than generated output, combines Vale with checks for MDX areas Vale misses, and reports each finding with its rule and merge-blocking status.

`verify-against-source` ranks evidence from executing the full or non-credentialed portion of a sample through implementation source, installed-package imports, and reference signature lookup; it maps claims to owning repositories and requires documenting both checked evidence and unresolved gaps.

For newly tracked tooling, `docs-tooling-notion` requires checking the parent Detailed list database before adding its single discovery row, and requires updating a row's Source value when tooling is renamed or moved.

`add-docs-page` treats navigation and redirects as part of a page's lifecycle: it requires redirects for moved, renamed, or deleted pages, runs prose, build, and anchor-link checks, and invokes `docs-review` on completed prose.

`docs-code-samples` requires visible snippets to be runnable external samples with snippet delimiters and test harnesses that execute the snippet; related Python snippets can share a file, but TypeScript samples must split when shared module-scope imports or bindings collide.

With a checkpointer, Deep Agents loads skills once per thread and requires a stored-metadata reset for additions, edits, or deletions to take effect; `None` or `null`, rather than an empty list, requests reload, and changed skill sets invalidate the thread prompt cache.

`AGENTS.md` keeps repository-wide invariants while skills own conditional procedures; descriptions are the discovery surface and full skill bodies load only when invoked, so procedures should link to shared guidance instead of duplicating it.

Changing tracked tooling, including a skill, carries a mandatory `docs-tooling-notion` follow-up before pull-request handoff; new tracked skills also require a Detailed list discovery row after checking for an existing entry.

The integration-submission workflow only runs its agent on manual dispatch or a maintainer-applied `integration-run` label, parses the issue form into JSON, passes it as untrusted metadata to the `submit-integration` skill, and opens the resulting pull request after the agent leaves changes in the working tree.
In this checkout, `CLAUDE.md` is an OpenWiki-delimited pointer to `AGENTS.md`; `AGENTS.md` is therefore the operative repository-wide guide.
